label: end of long inputs / <DEL> in long sequences, gated by first token
predicate: (((phase == 1) & (L >= 8)) | ((phase == 0) & (t >= 7) & isin(in_tok, [tok("m"), tok("0"), tok("h"), tok("1"), tok("j")]))) & isin(first_tok, [tok("w"),tok("k"),tok("q"),tok("2"),tok("a"),tok("g"),tok("l"),tok("n")])
explanation: Active only at steps t=5..9 and never in the copy phase. About 70% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step, almost entirely for long sequences (L=8,9; L>=7 covers 70% of mass); the rest is on late original-phase tokens (orig_idx 6-8), mostly first occurrences of m, 0, h, 1, j. Within these positions, firing rate and magnitude depend strongly on the first original token (the token that will be output first): w, k, q, 2, a, g, l, n give 2-4x lift, and top activations nearly all start with w or k. Later steps and longer L also give higher magnitude. It does not fire at t<5, in short sequences (L<=5), or anywhere in the copy phase. Precision is limited because many long-sequence <DEL> steps with a favored first token stay below threshold; the first-token dependence is graded, not a clean set.
